question: Formalize a finite one-dimensional periodic lattice with sites ZMod N, N positive, real positions and momenta, strictly positive site masses, the forward difference operator D q i = q (i+1) - q i, and basic finite-sum identities. Prove only finite-dimensional algebraic facts. Use Mathlib and inspect Physlib.CondensedMatter.LatticeModels.Basic for reusable grounded definitions; do not assume thermalization or localization.

For the finite periodic random-mass lattice, formalize the diagonal mass and inverse-mass operators from a strictly positive mass function. Prove the inverse-mass identities, positivity of the kinetic quadratic form, and the mass-weighted coordinate algebra needed later. Ground against Mathlib matrix and inner-product APIs and Physlib units/mass APIs; no probabilistic localization theorem is requested.

Formalize the finite nonlinear lattice Hamiltonian H = sum_i [p_i^2/(2 m_i) + (Dq_i)^2/2 + lambda/n*(Dq_i)^n] for n at least 3. Prove the exact algebraic rescaling q=sqrt(epsilon) q_tilde, p=sqrt(epsilon) p_tilde under explicit positivity and real-power hypotheses, identifying effective coupling g=lambda*epsilon^((n-2)/2) and the algebraic identity g^(-2)=lambda^(-2)*epsilon^(-(n-2)) under required nonzero assumptions. This identity must not be presented as a proof of a thermalization time law. Ground Hamiltonian notions against Physlib.ClassicalMechanics.HamiltonsEquations.

For the linear lambda=0 finite lattice, define the mass-weighted real symmetric dynamical matrix Phi=M^(-1/2) D^* D M^(-1/2). Prove self-adjointness and nonnegativity in finite dimension and state a faithful normal-mode diagonalization interface with the translation zero mode treated explicitly. Prove harmonic modal-energy conservation only from a stated harmonic-flow equation. Do not claim infinite-volume Anderson localization.

Formalize nonnegative harmonic modal energies on a nonempty finite monitored mode set, late-window averages for 0 <= mu < 1 and T>0, normalized modal weights, and approximate equipartition as L1 distance to the uniform probability vector. Prove normalization and elementary distance bounds. Use Mathlib finite sums and interval integrals; consult Physlib statistical mechanics and thermodynamics definitions without replacing the observable by an equilibrium axiom.

Define spectral entropy of a finite normalized nonnegative modal-energy vector using the convention 0*log 0=0, entropy deficit, and participation number. Prove near-term elementary properties that are supported by Mathlib, including nonnegativity and the value at the uniform vector; separate harder entropy-distance inequalities into explicitly stated future lemmas rather than adding axioms.

Define the equilibration first hitting time as an extended nonnegative real infimum of positive times satisfying approximate equipartition, with infinity when the set is empty, plus a persistence-time predicate over an interval. Prove basic order and membership consequences of sInf under explicit nonemptiness hypotheses. Do not define hitting time by equality to a floating-point threshold.

Formalize a conditional effective kinetic evolution whose vector field is g^2 times a collision operator independent of g. Under explicit existence and uniqueness and g nonzero assumptions, prove the exact solution time rescaling D_g(t)=D_1(g^2*t), then derive the corresponding compatible hitting-time scaling. Clearly label this as a theorem about the effective kinetic model, not a derivation from the microscopic disordered lattice. Define the microscopic T_eq asymptotic scaling only as a named conjecture Prop with no axiom and no proof obligation.
